title: Biaxial Mechanical Characterizations of Atrioventricular Heart Valves
protocol: Retrieve animal hearts on the same day as slaughter and store in an ice chest.
Transport the hearts to the laboratory space.
Submerge the heart in a bucket of PBS solution to rinse off excess blood.
Lay a placemat on the dissection counter for easy cleanup.
Place the rinsed heart on the placemat.
Locate the parting line between the atria and ventricle using forceps.
Make an incision along the parting line with a razor blade to reveal heart valves and ventricles.
Incise the entire outer circumference of the heart to remove the atria and all material superior to the ventricles.
With forceps, carefully pull out any observed blood clots in the ventricles.
Rinse the heart one final time in a bucket with PBS solution.
Place the clean heart in the plastic bag and store it in a freezer.
Mix the blood with a bleach solution of 10% bleach and 90% water.
Stir the mixture continuously for approximately 10 min.
Dispose of the bleach-treated blood through drainage.
Make an incision along the commissure and carefully cut through the ventricular wall.
Cut the chordal attachments to fully open the ventricle if necessary.
Open the ventricle once the full incision is made.
Identify the MV anterior and posterior leaflets.
Sever the chordal attachments of the leaflets to the papillary muscles using a surgical blade.
Stretch the leaflets taut with forceps and make cuts to separate them from the annulus.
Place excised leaflets in an appropriately labeled container filled with PBS solution.
Store the container with leaflets in a refrigerator at approximately 4 °C.
Hold the heart for a top-down view and identify the TV on the right side of the heart.
Make an incision through one of the commissures and the ventricular wall to locate the TV.
Identify the TV septal, posterior, and anterior leaflets.
Perform leaflet extraction as done in step 2.4.
Place all obtained leaflets in a labeled container filled with PBS solution.
Store the container in a refrigerator at approximately 4 °C.
Retrieve a leaflet from the fridge for tissue dissection.
Prepare a tissue cutter for the specified sectioning size.
Use a surgical pen, forceps, razor blades, and a cutting mat for further processing.
Using forceps, remove the specimen from the PBS solution.
Lay the specimen flat on the cutting mat with the radial direction aligned to the Y-direction and the circumferential direction aligned to the X-direction.
Identify the leaflet’s central region as the testing section.
Align the tissue cutter so that the desired tissue testing region is within the boundaries of the razor blades.
Make one horizontal cut and another vertical cut to form a square region of the desired dimensions.
Using the surgical pen, label the tissue’s radial direction.
Trim any chordal attachments by stretching the chordae from the leaflet with forceps and making a careful cut without causing damage to the leaflet.
Retrieve the sectioned tissue specimen, digital calipers, and a small metal spatula.
Measure and record the thickness of the metal spatula using the digital calipers.
Using forceps, lay the tissue specimen flat on the metal spatula.
Measure the thickness of the spatula-tissue pair at three different leaflet locations using digital calipers.
Subtract the spatula’s thickness from each measurement and record the average thickness.
Prepare a PBS bath at 37 °C.
Retrieve forceps, the tissue specimen, mounting hardware, a fine-tipped tool, glass beads (with diameters of 300–500 µm), and super glue.
Mount the tissue to the biaxial testing system.
Ensure that the tissue’s circumferential and radial directions are aligned with the machine’s X- and Y-directions.
Place a small pool of super glue in one container and glass beads into another container.
Coat the tip of a fine-tipped tool with a small amount of super glue.
Stick an individual bead to the tip of the tool.
Transfer the bead carefully to one corner of the middle third of the tissue’s testing region.
Repeat this step until a square array of four beads is formed.

Create a preconditioning protocol so that the tissue will undergo 10 loading/unloading cycles at forces associated with peak membrane tension at a loading rate of 4.42 N/min, including a preload of 2.5% of the maximum force.
Establish a loading rate of 4.42 N/min for subsequent testing.
Create a new set of testing parameters.
Set the name of the protocol as Preconditioning0.
For the X- and Y-axes, set the control mode to be force.
Set the control function to be step.
Set the load magnitude as the force associated with targeted peak membrane tension.
Set the preload magnitude as 2.5% of the maximum force for the first repetition only.
Set the stretch duration to be 25 seconds.
Set the recovery duration to be 25 seconds.
Set the number of repetitions to be 10.
Make a note of the tissue’s deformation in the X- and Y-directions after preconditioning.
Prepare a protocol to move the specimen to the maximum force, beginning from the recorded size.
Retrieve a stopwatch for timing purposes.
Begin the maximum force loading protocol.
Start the stopwatch simultaneously when the machine begins actuation.
Stop the stopwatch when the actuation stops.
Record the post-preconditioning peak tissue deformation.
Represent the tissue’s optimal stretch time using the stopwatch reading.
Prepare a force-controlled protocol at a loading rate of 4.42 N/min.
Open a new testing directory and name the test.
Set the data to save to a known location for use in later stress and strain calculations.
Move the specimen back to the original mounting configuration.
Create a protocol set titled FirstImage.
Set the X-axis and Y-axis control mode to force.
Set the control function to step.
Set the load magnitude to 0 mN.
Set the stretch duration to 1 second.
Set the recovery duration to 1 second.
Set the number of repetitions to 1.
Set the data output frequency to 1 Hz.
Set the image output frequency to 1 Hz.
Construct a new testing set named PreconditioningA.
Establish testing parameters for cyclic loading/unloading with 10 repetitions.
Set stretch time and recovery time as recorded previously.
Do not capture images in the A testing set.
Capture data at 15 Hz during A testing set.
Construct another testing set named PreconditioningB.
All testing parameters should be identical to those of PreconditioningA.
Set image output frequency to 15 Hz for PreconditioningB.
Do not apply preload for PreconditioningB.
Create testing protocols to load tissue to peak membrane tension at a loading rate of 4.42 N/min with ratios: 1:1, 0.75:1, 1:0.75, 0.5:1, and 1:0.5.
Retrieve data from the last two cycles of each loading ratio for subsequent analyses.
Prepare a displacement-controlled testing protocol at a loading rate of 4.42 N/min.
Biaxially stretch the sample in the X-direction and Y-direction to the displacements associated with peak circumferential and radial stretches, respectively.
Construct a rest cycle of 1 min that holds the tissue at its original mounted configuration after each step.
Perform pure shear along the X-direction by stretching in the X-direction for peak circumferential stretch and shortening in the Y-direction while keeping the dashed area constant under deformation.
Conduct constrained uniaxial stretching along the X-direction.
Execute pure shear along the Y-direction.
Carry out constrained uniaxial stretching along the Y-direction.
Retrieve data from the last two cycles of each loading ratio for analysis.
Prepare a stress-relaxation protocol with a loading rate of 4.42 N/min to load the tissue in each direction to the displacements associated with peak membrane tensions.
Hold the tissue at that displacement for 15 min during the stress-relaxation test.
After 15 min, recover the tissue to its original mounting configuration.
Abort the test immediately if tissue tearing occurs to prevent potential damage.
Unmount the tissue from the biaxial testing system.
Place the tissue into a container filled with 10% formalin.
Store the container in a refrigerated environment at approximately 4 °C.
Fix the tissue for 24–48 hours, depending on its thickness.
Transfer the fixed tissue to an 80% ethanol solution.
Store the tissue in solution in a refrigerated environment at 4 °C.
Prepare the tissue for commercial histology analysis as per the vendor’s instructions.
Using ImageJ, perform color deconvolution methods to determine the percentage of each stained constituent in the tissue.
Perform DIC-based tracking on the four fiducial markers from the images taken during biaxial mechanical testing to determine the time-dependent marker positions.
Let XI be the marker positions in the undeformed state at the beginning of the biaxial test or at the end of the preconditioning protocol, depending on the reference configuration chosen.
Compute the deformation gradient (F) of the fiducial markers using a four-node bilinear finite element method.
Compute the right Cauchy–Green deformation tensor (C) and the Green strain tensor (E).
Determine the circumferential and radial stretches by taking the square roots of the principle values of C.
Determine the first Piola-Kirchhoff (1st-PK) stress tensor (P).
Compute other stress tensors, such as the Cauchy stress tensor (σ) and the second Piola-Kirchoff (2nd-PK) stress tensor (S).
